title: Two survivors miraculously rescued 10 days after devastating flash floods in Nepal - CNN
description: Two survivors miraculously rescued 10 days after devastating flash floods in Nepal  CNN
publisher.title: CNN
full_article:
Two more survivors from Nepal’s catastrophic flash floods were rescued on Saturday, offering a sliver of hope for a region reeling from the destruction wrought by a wave of water, ice and mud that washed away entire riverside communities 10 days ago.

A Chinese national, Lu Haitao, was pulled from the hydropower tunnels where hundreds of other workers remain missing while the other, 60-year-old Chandika Shrestha, was found downriver, on the upper floor of a four-story building in the devastated community of Betrawati.

So much time has passed since the floods that Shrestha’s family had started ceremonial last rites and begun preparing for her funeral, believing she had died, a local official said.

Thousands of families remain in this limbo across Nepal and China, not knowing if their loved ones are alive or dead. At least 1,362 people are known to have died in the disaster, authorities say.

About 900 of those missing are hydropower workers, who were working at facilities dotted along the Trishuli River when a huge chunk of ice sheared off a melting glacier, triggering a landslide and floods which buried entire communities in minutes.

Lu said he had been desperately trying to attract rescue workers’ attention for days, crying for help whenever he saw their lights.

“Whenever I saw the lights, I shouted, ‘Hey!’ Really loudly, really loudly,’ he told Chinese state broadcaster CCTV. “Maybe they didn’t hear me.

“When they came to rescue me today, even when their (lights) were shining right in front of me, I couldn’t believe it.”

Nepal Army

Two other workers were rescued on Friday from a different hydropower plant after rescuers had worked around the clock in treacherous conditions in the hope of finding survivors.

But away from these miraculous rescues, the death toll continues to rise – two bodies were recovered from the same site where Lu was found – and other families are still enduring an agonizing wait for news of missing relatives.

Krishna Poudel added an image of his younger brother Ishwor, a 26-year-old hydropower worker, to a board with scores of other such posters for those missing eight days ago, but he still doesn’t know his brother’s fate.

Some who escaped from the tunnels told Poudel that his brother is still inside, he told Reuters. “They said they could hear the voices of about 200-300 people shouting from inside,” he said.

Related article Nepal army soldiers work during a search and rescue operation outside a tunnel near the Hydropower Project sites in Rasuwa district, Nepal, in this handout obtained on September 2. NEPAL ARMY/Handout/Reuters ‘Don’t panic’: How two men were rescued from a flood-stricken Nepali power plant 5 min read

Rescue teams, helped by specialist crews from other countries including India and China, are concentrating their efforts on these hydropower stations. But authorities are also working to rescue those who found themselves cut off by the floods and to rebuild temporary bridges across the river, the Nepali Army said Saturday.

More than 7,500 homes across Nepal and around 55 kilometers (34 miles) of road were damaged in the floods, the Nepali Foreign Ministry said Saturday, leaving thousands in need of humanitarian assistance but with access to the area severely restricted.

Around 35,000 people are believed to need safe temporary accommodation, while 43,000 are feared to be at immediate risk of food insecurity, according to a United Nations report.

With such urgent humanitarian assistance required, dozens of US Congress members have written to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, calling on him and his department to “do much more.” That, they suggested, should include providing daily updates to family members of missing Americans, share aerial imagery with first responders, and provide additional reconstruction support.

A State Department spokesperson told CNN “we do not comment on Congressional correspondence.” They pointed to the $3.6 million already committed to the relief effort, and said an additional $3 million in assistance “will be provided through our global assistance award with World Food Programme.”

full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued on Friday.

Nepal's army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-meter (about 740-foot) tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man, called Lu Haitao, out of the tunnel.

CCTV shared audio of Lu talking to an officer, saying how he repeatedly shouted whenever he saw the rescue crews’ lights, but they could not hear him.

“When they rescued me today, when they shone (the light) before my eyes, I couldn’t believe it,” he said.

Lu was taken to a hospital and was in stable condition, according to CCTV.

googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('JGFI_Article2_300x250'); });

Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing and roughly 500 are believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said. Specialized rescue ​teams from India, China, South Korea and the United States have been searching through debris, damaged structures and tunnels at the projects, hoping to find survivors.

In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.

Images released by Nepal’s army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket.

At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

Saaliq reported from New Delhi. Associated Press journalist Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.

A Plymouth, Massachusetts, restaurant owner is grieving the loss of his family members during the deadly flooding in Nepal.

Kaisang Ghale owns the Lobster Hut on Plymouth Harbor. He grew up in Nepal before moving to the South Shore.

.css-3qk0ue{margin:0 24px 0 0;position:relative;z-index:100;}@media only screen and (min-width: 61.25rem){.css-3qk0ue{clear:left;float:left;min-width:300px;max-width:336px;}}

Ghale told NewsCenter 5 he lost friends and close family members when flooding broke out in his home country in late August.

Others in his village ran for their lives as water overtook vehicles and homes. Ghale and his wife woke up to a phone call from his cousins as the disaster unfolded.

"He said, 'Then we ran uphill,' back of his house is uphill so they ran as much as they could and his and his wife survived, his older sister was behind his wife; she couldn't make it, so these are the stories that I've heard from him," said Ghale. "It's almost like a nightmare, and I still- I'm still... hard to believe."

He said his family's village is a small one.

Ghale is raising money in response to the disaster and is planning to go there next week. The funds will be used for food, water, medical supplies, and temporary housing for the victims, according to Ghale's GoFundMe.

title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster - The Guardian
description: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.

The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.

Rescue efforts have focused on a dozen hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing, 500 of whom are thought to be trapped in huge tunnels. International rescue teams from India, China, South Korea and the US have been searching through debris and damaged structures at the projects to try to find survivors.

Two Nepali workers were rescued from another tunnel in a hydro-station on the Trishuli River on Friday.

Rescue of Nepal hydropower workers ‘triumph for humans and humanity’, tunnelling expert says Read more

Experts have said the possibility of finding missing people alive in the tunnels is diminishing.

The Nepali woman, 64, was rescued from a damaged house in the devastated town of Nuwakot. Photos published by the Nepali army showed rescuers discovering the woman submerged in mud before she was pulled to safety and airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.



Members of Nepal’s police force cheered as she was pulled from the home, the lower half of which was buried in thick sludge.

Emergency responders have been working to find survivors from the devastating floods in Nepal, which were triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on 26 August. Their work has been complicated by the massive infrastructural damage caused by the floods, with more than 40 bridges having collapsed and rivers swelling unpredictably.

At least 1,375 people have been killed in the floods, with more than 5,000 missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

विध्वंसित शहर नुवाकोटके क्षतिग्रस्त घरसँ ६४ वर्षीय नेपाली महिलाके उद्धार कएल गेल अछि । नेपाली सेना द्वारा प्रकाशित फोटो मे बचावकर्मी के महिला के थाल मे डूबल पता चलल अछि, ओकरा बाद ओकरा सुरक्षित स्थान पर खींच क इलाज के लेल हवाई जहाज सं काठमांडू पहुंचा देल गेल।



घर सँ खींचैत नेपालक पुलिस बलक सदस्य सभ जय-जयकार करैत छल, जकर निचला आधा भाग मोट कीचड़ मे गाड़ल छल ।

26 अगस्त कए हिमनदी आ चट्टान गिरला स नेपाल मे आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि स बचि गेल लोक कए खोजबा मे इमरजेंसी रिस्पांसर काज करैत आबि रहल अछि। बाढ़ि सं भेल भारी बुनियादी ढांचागत नुकसान के कारण हुनकर काज जटिल भ गेल अछि, जाहि मे 40 सं बेसी पुल ढहि गेल अछि आओर नदी अप्रत्याशित रूप सं फूलि गेल अछि.

नेपाल के आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार बाढ़ि मे कम सं कम 1375 लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि, जाहि मे 5000 सं बेसि लोक लापता अछि.

full_article:

Over 100 people gathered for a candlelight vigil to honor people who died or are missing from the Aug. 26 flash flood in Nepal , raising money for ongoing search and relief efforts in Santa Rosa on Tuesday.

Sonoma County community members gathered on the west side of Old Courthouse Square holding hand-written signs of support and Nepali flags. Attendees arranged candles to spell the words “Pray for Nepal” and to outline the country’s red, white and blue two-pointed flag.

As of Sept. 5, 2026,1,344 people are confirmed dead with over 5,000 still missing in Nepal, 21 people are reported dead and over 500 more are missing in Tibet, and over 13,000 people have been successfully rescued from the flood, according to India Today .

Kyan KC, a SRJC computer science student, attended the vigil with his mother. He has not been able to get in contact with friends and family in Nepal since the disaster occurred.

“The rain is still going on; I’ve got no replies from them, nor their families,” Kyan KC said. “I’ve tried texting their sisters, their cousins, their own family members; no reply from them.”

With the start of the fall semester, Kyan KC said he has worked to complete his schoolwork quickly so that he can focus on the needs in Nepal. He kept himself updated on the situation, shared information on his Instagram page, donated and prayed.

SRJC computer science student Kyan KC wonders if his family and friends are safe during the Condolence and Candlelight Gathering for Nepal at OId Courthouse Square in Santa Rosa on Sept. 1, 2026. (Pacific Jeremy)

“So I plan on doing some more, I’m trying to get people to organize community so we can put all the money together and then send it all back to Nepal,” Kyan KC said.

Three Sonoma County mayors attended the vigil at the invitation of the United Nepalese of California, the group who organized the event. Mark Stapp of Santa Rosa, Rosa Reynoza of Windsor, and Emily Sanborn of Rohnert Park.

Sanborn, dressed in an “I heart Rohnert Park” sweatshirt said, “We have a foundation through the City of Rohnert Park. So we do grants every other year for non-profits as long as they are doing something to benefit the community, and so I want to make sure the UNC is applying for that grant when it opens up later this year.”

Dual-enrolled SRJC and Santa Rosa High School student who identified with his last name, Biplovwagle, spent much of the event collecting donations. He expressed the importance of donating to the crowd and explained that there is over $5 billion in damages, roughly a tenth of Nepal’s annual GDP.

The funds raised will be sent to the Government of Nepal Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund.

“ The Government of Nepal makes a sincere appeal to all citizens, organizations, and institutions to provide financial support to the Prime Minister’s Natural Disaster Relief Fund and the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers,” a disaster relief appeal from the Government of Nepal’s official website stated.

Manoj Thaugunna of UNC said that donation bins will be placed at local Nepali-owned businesses to collect cash donations for the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund. According to a list Thaugunna provided to The Oak Leaf, donation box locations include Darbar Kitchen Indian & Nepalese Cuisine and NeilMed Pharmaceuticals in Santa Rosa, Kathmandu Smoke Shop and West Coast Sourdough in Rohnert Park, and Batika Indian Bistro in Novato.

The vigil replaced a previously scheduled Haritalika festival for women originally planned to be held at the Veterans Memorial Building, said Deepak Timsina, president of UNC.

“In light of the devastating floods and natural disasters in Nepal, which have caused significant loss of life, property, and immense suffering to our fellow Nepalis, we are deeply saddened and heartbroken,” the UNC stated in the Teej cancellation notice . “At a time when many of our brothers, sisters, families and communities in Nepal are facing such pain and hardship, we feel that it would not be appropriate to celebrate our festival as usual.”

Laurie Fong and Grace Cheung-Schulman, president and vice-president of the Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition of North Bay, initially planned to attend the Teej ceremony, but attended the vigil instead.

“It’s all about humanity, and if we really put our humanity foot forward, we’re all connected,” Fong said before the ceremony began. She said the Nepalese community is one of the fastest growing ethnic groups in the area.

Attendees stand in solidarity with the victims of the Aug. 26 flash flood in Nepal during the Condolence and Candlelight Gathering for Nepal at OId Courthouse Square in Santa Rosa on Sept. 1, 2026. (Pacific Jeremy)

“From India, a lot of people go to Mansarovar as a pilgrimage, so a lot of Indian people are gone missing there too,” Ruk Sundaramurdhy said before the vigil on Tuesday.

Sundaramurdhy is a member of the North Bay Hindu Center, located in Petaluma. He explained that the affected area in Nepal lies between India and two important pilgrimage sites in Tibet.

“Once in a lifetime everybody has to go take that pilgrimage,” Sundaramurdhy said about the two Hindu pilgrimage sites, Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar.

Despite the uncertainty, attendees remained hopeful. “Right now they are missing, so there is no dead body found or anything, but there is some hope. Until the body is found dead, people always have some hope,” Suman Ghimire said about the people still missing.

Two people were rescued in separate operations on Saturday as Nepal continues dealing with the fallout from devastating floods that hit the country 10 days ago.

The Nepali military said Saturday a team made up of its army and South Korean disaster experts saved a Chinese man from a 740 foot tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, The Guardian reported. CNN wrote that a 60-year-old Nepali woman was found downriver in a four-story building in Betrawati.

A local official said the family of the woman, Chandika Shrestha, started ceremonial last rites and preparations for her funeral, as they thought she died, according to CNN.

Authorities said at least 1,362 people died due to the flooding. Around 900 hydropower workers at facilities near the Trishuli River are among the thousands of missing.

On Friday, rescuers pulled two workers, a mechanical foreman and a supervisor, alive from a tunnel in the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant. Both were reportedly in stable condition, and taken to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment.

Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, the head of the Nepal Electricity Authority, said that a third man’s body was recovered at the hydropower plant, too, The New York Times wrote. The man was a mechanical engineer, he said.

Rescuers said they heard voices from inside the tunnel on Friday morning, which helped them locate the workers. More voices can still be heard inside, the rescuers said.

The flash floods and mudslides began after a glacial collapse near the Nepal–China border on Aug. 26.

Nepal’s Foreign Ministry says a preliminary assessment conducted under the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment shows about 7,570 houses were damaged, affecting 32,933 people. Another 48 government officers were affected, as well as 34 miles of roads, 37 drivable bridges and 68 suspension bridges.

Around 4,462 acres of agricultural land, 13 hydropower projects, one solar power plant and two transmission lines were damaged as well, the Foreign Ministry said in a Saturday update.

“Given the scale and extent of the damage caused by this disaster, a comprehensive Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) is being simultaneously undertaken to determine the full extent of loss and damage and the costs for rebuilding and reconstruction,” Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said.

सीएनएन के अनुसार, एक स्थानीय अधिकारी कहलनि जे, महिला के परिवार चंडिका श्रेष्ठ हुनकर अंतिम संस्कार के लेल विधिवत अंतिम संस्कार आ तैयारी शुरू केलक, कियाक त हुनका सब के लागल जे हुनकर मौत भ गेल अछि।

जे कहानी महत्व रखै छै ओकरा हेरफेर, पूर्वाग्रह या एजेंडा स॑ मुक्त करै लेली आज ही सीधा तीर ऐप डाउनलोड करी क॑ देखै ल॑ मिलतै ।TM फोन कैमरा क॑ यहाँ इशारा करी क॑ देखै ल॑ मिलतै

अधिकारि सब के कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि के कारण कम सं कम 1362 लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि. त्रिशूली नदी क समीप सुविधा पर करीब 900 जलविद्युत मजदूर हजारों लापता मे शामिल छथि।

शुक्रदिन बचावकर्मी त्रिशुली 3ए जलविद्युत संयंत्र मे सुरंग स दूटा मजदूर, एकटा यांत्रिक फोरमैन आ एकटा सुपरवाइजर कए जीवित खींच लेलक। दुनु के हालत स्थिर बताओल जा रहल अछि, आ इलाज के लेल काठमांडू के अस्पताल पहुंचाओल गेल अछि.

नेपाल विद्युत प्राधिकरणके प्रमुख दिर्घायु कुमार श्रेष्ठ जलविद्युत संयंत्रमे सेहो तेसर आदमीके शव बरामद भेल जानकारी द न्यूयॉर्क टाइम्स लिखने अछि । ओ कहलनि जे, ओ आदमी मैकेनिकल इंजीनियर छल।

बचावकर्मी के कहनाय छनि जे शुक्रदिन भोर मे सुरंग के अंदर सं आवाज सुनल गेल, जाहि सं मजदूर के पता लगाबय मे मदद मिलल. बचावकर्मी कहलनि जे, भीतर एखनो आओर आवाज सुनबा मे आबि रहल अछि।

26 अगस्त कए नेपाल-चीन सीमाक समीप हिमनदी ध्वस्त भेलाक बाद आकस्मिक बाढ़ि आ कीचड़क स्खलन शुरू भेल छल ।

नेपाल के विदेश मंत्रालय के कहनाय छनि जे रैपिड डेमेज एंड नीड्स असेसमेंट के तहत कएल गेल प्रारंभिक आकलन मे करीब 7570 घर क्षतिग्रस्त भेल अछि जाहि सं 32,933 लोक प्रभावित भेल अछि. 48टा आओर सरकारी अधिकारी प्रभावित भेलाह, संगहि 34 मील सड़क, 37 ड्राइव करय योग्य पुल आ 68 झूला पुल सेहो प्रभावित भेलाह।

विदेश मंत्रालय शनिदिन जारी अपडेट मे कहलक अछि जे करीब 4,462 एकड़ कृषि भूमि, 13 जलविद्युत परियोजना, एकटा सौर ऊर्जा संयंत्र आ दूटा संचरण लाइन सेहो क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि।

For Jeena Gurung Vomhof, the Minnesota State Fair was supposed to be a celebration.

A chance to share the art and traditions of the country she still calls home.

Then came devastating news from Nepal.

"I was almost done with the set up to be selling at the 2026 Minnesota State Fair. Excited, pumped, you know, new space, new energy, and I couldn't, I couldn't see my social media, like what's happening. It was like, that was not real to me. And I just called my mom and said what's happening," said Gurung Vomhof.

Gurung Vomhof is originally from Kathmandu.

Nepal is home to Gurung Vomhof's family, her memories, and the women whose work she brings to Minnesota.

"Nepal is a beautiful country. It's an Asian country, right below China and above India, surrounded by beautiful mountains, beautiful people, the tradition, the culture, the love, the humanity that is there in the country I still miss and I try to bring that wherever I go," explained Gurung Vomhof.

Through her business, Namaste Brows & Boutique in Roseville, Gurung Vomhof employs sixteen women in Nepalmaking — hand-crafted earrings, cashmere shawls, hemp, and felt gift items. 100% of the proceeds go back to the makers.

"Each and every piece that I sell has a story," said Gurung Vomhof.

But right now, she's carrying a story of loss.

"My friends, my family, who are far and close, are still back home and we have lost two cousins, 21 and 35, who were going trekking. They're missing," said Gurung Vomhof

She talks with family every day, trying to stay connected while holding herself together.

At the fair, people she doesn't know are giving her something she needs right now.

"My favorite thing right now is hugs. You know, when I'm holding all of this, I don't know how, I have the right word physically, emotionally.

Joy, hurt? That hug means so much," said Gurung Vomhof

Those moments are helping her keep going.

She's already thinking beyond the immediate crisis - about children, education, and rebuilding.

"Education is the root of everything, everything. For me, maybe I can build a classroom, but I can't do it alone. I need all of you," said Gurung Vomhof.

For now, she'll keep standing for Nepal, sharing its culture, and believing in the people standing with her.

"I am at the grandstand at the lower level, row number nine, wide open with colors, with joy, and I'm going to be standing here every single minute," said Gurung Vomhof.

full_article:
Rescuers transfer a worker rescued alive in Rasuwa district, Nepal, Sept 4, 2026. Two men trapped inside the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project, which was badly affected by last week's deadly mudslide, were rescued alive on Friday, the Nepali Army said. (HANDOUT/NEPALI ARMY VIA XINHUA)

BEIJING – China is stepping up meteorological support for Nepal following last week's mudslide disaster, providing satellite data and meteorological services to assist cross-border disaster monitoring and emergency response, according to the China Meteorological Administration (CMA).

The administration has been providing Nepal with a range of meteorological products through MAZU, China's AI-powered meteorological early warning solution, including multi-source satellite data and products from the Fengyun-3 and Fengyun-4 meteorological satellite series.

ALSO READ: Police: Nepal mudslide death toll reaches 1,344

On Aug 26, a severe mudslide struck the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing between China and Nepal.

China's National Satellite Meteorological Center has continued to monitor precipitation and weather changes in the disaster-affected areas. China has also used high-resolution satellite data to track upstream ice-rock avalanche areas and river channels, supporting disaster assessment, rescue and meteorological services.

The CMA has connected Nepal-customized services to China's Fengyun meteorological satellites in real time. They enable real-time monitoring of convective weather and lightning activity, helping Nepal track precipitation conditions and severe convective weather over a wider area.

READ MORE: Searches near Gyirong Port now deeper, more targeted

Since the disaster occurred, Chinese meteorological and water resources authorities have maintained close cooperation with their Nepali counterparts, sharing monitoring information and jointly responding to the disaster, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Thursday.

China will continue to strengthen cooperation with Nepal in relevant fields and provide strong support for Nepal's emergency rescue and response efforts, Guo added.
